{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the very start because its outline is made of gentle curves that dominoes handle well, and I drew the full sketch on the pad within the first minute. That sketch was the blueprint the whole table built from. I laid the start domino and the top line from the nose, and I carried the line on from the crossing out to the upper tail tip. By my inspection, nearly all of the standing dominoes (about 121 of 124) were connected to the start before the push.

Execution: I built from the pad so the shape matched the plan. I then inspected the tail and the crossing, which is the riskiest spot in the design, and confirmed the chain carried through. I decided to leave the three pale strays alone since they sat against the live line. After that I kept my hands off the table so nobody would bump it before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work at the outset: I took the top line, Omar the bottom line, and Hana and Jack the tail. I coordinated with Hana so we weren't waiting on each other at the crossing, and I told Jack how to judge the doubled-up joint. I called for hands off once the inspection came back clean.

Leadership: I set the direction early by choosing the animal, producing the sketch and assigning roles, so the table never stalled on what to build. I kept the group aligned on a simple rule: finish, verify, then stop touching. I led the hands-off discipline for the final minutes. The table finished with a clean, connected fish and no stray rework.", "my_share_percent": 40}
